newsitem.title: USA: Entergy postpones Arkansas nuke startup.
newsitem.headline: Entergy postpones Arkansas nuke startup.

text.p: Entergy Corp has postponed the restart of its 836 megawatt (MW) Arkansas nuclear power unit 1 and now expects to begin electricity production this Thursday, a company spokesman said Monday.
"We expect to begin heatup later today, and we expect to be tied to the grid on Thursday," spokesman Terry Young said.
The Russellville, Ark., unit was originally expected to restart October 20 from a scheduled maintenance and refueling outage which began September 12.
Startup of the unit was delayed while the company repaired damage caused by an insulation fire at the unit last Thursday, Young said.
Damage from the fire was relatively minimal, he said.
Separately, Entergy's 1,173 MW Grand Gulf nuclear power unit 1 was shut down October 19 as expected for 32 days of scheduled refueling and maintenance, Young said.
The Port Gibson, Miss., unit was expected to return to service Nov 21.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
